title: La meilleure alternative à Fiddler
description:
Fiddler a gagné deux décennies de bonne volonté en tant que proxy de débogage Windows gratuit : il montrait chaque requête émise par votre machine, depuis n'importe quelle application, déchiffrée. Ce Fiddler s'appelle désormais Fiddler Classic, et la page de Telerik décrit son état sans détour : Windows uniquement, usage non commercial uniquement, mode maintenance, avec « aucun engagement pour les versions, correctifs ou support technique ». Le successeur pris en charge, Fiddler Everywhere, est multiplateforme et actif, mais c'est un abonnement : selon la page de tarification Telerik, Lite est à 7 $ par utilisateur et par mois en facturation annuelle (10 $ en mensuel), Pro à 13 $ (19 $ en mensuel) et Enterprise à 37 $, annuel uniquement. Il y a un essai de 10 jours et aucun niveau gratuit.

Essayez Apidog dès aujourd'hui

Le « Fiddler gratuit » a donc disparu pour quiconque l'utilise au travail, et la question honnête du remplacement se divise en deux. Fiddler est un proxy MITM à l'échelle du système, et Apidog n'en est pas un — cet article ne prétendra pas le contraire. Mais regardez comment la plupart des développeurs utilisaient réellement Fiddler : composer des requêtes contre leur propre API, inspecter les réponses, simuler un backend avec des règles AutoResponder. C'est du travail de client API déguisé en proxy, et pour cette part du travail, Apidog est l'outil conçu pour cela : un client de requêtes complet, un serveur mock intelligent à la place des règles AutoResponder, des points de terminaison documentés, des tests automatisés, gratuit jusqu'à 4 utilisateurs. Pour une véritable capture de trafic, les bonnes réponses sont les outils de capture comme mitmproxy, nommés honnêtement plus bas.

Qu'est-il arrivé à Fiddler

Deux produits partagent maintenant ce nom, et aucun n'est l'ancien contrat.

Fiddler Classic reste un téléchargement gratuit, mais lisez les petits caractères : usage non commercial uniquement, Windows uniquement, mode maintenance sans versions, correctifs ou support promis. Il est antérieur à HTTP/2 et à gRPC. Si vous déboguez des API d'entreprise avec, vous êtes hors licence ; si vous êtes sur Mac ou Linux, vous n'avez jamais fait partie du club.

Fiddler Everywhere est la version sur laquelle Telerik veut les professionnels : macOS, Linux et Windows, avec support HTTP/2, WebSockets, gRPC et SSE. Il a conservé les deux moitiés de l'ancien flux de travail : Compose Requests pour créer et enregistrer des appels API, et un moteur de règles (le successeur d'AutoResponder) pour modifier le trafic et simuler des réponses. Le piège, c'est le compteur. Les règles de modification du trafic et la collaboration d'équipe sont sur Pro à 13 $ par utilisateur et par mois ; Lite à 7 $ couvre la capture et l'inspection ; les contrôles Enterprise coûtent 37 $. Dix jours d'essai, puis la facture commence.

Rien de tout cela n'est un scandale ; maintenir un proxy de déchiffrement multiplateforme est un vrai travail. Mais cela change le calcul : vous ne décidez plus si vous gardez un outil gratuit, vous décidez quel outil payant mérite la place — et cela dépend du travail Fiddler que vous faisiez réellement.

Les deux tâches cachées dans Fiddler

Soyez précis sur votre propre usage avant de choisir un remplacement, car Fiddler regroupait deux tâches différentes :

Tâche 1 : capture de trafic. Vous devez voir les requêtes que vous ne contrôlez pas : les appels d'une application de bureau, l'API non documentée d'une application mobile, une session de navigateur déchiffrée. Cela nécessite un proxy MITM à l'échelle du système, avec installation de certificat. Apidog ne fait pas ce travail, et aucun client API ne le fait.

Tâche 2 : travail sur API. Vous construisez ou consommez une API que vous contrôlez. Vous composiez des requêtes, inspectiez les réponses, écriviez des règles AutoResponder pour que le front-end puisse se développer contre de fausses réponses, et rejouiez des sessions pour reproduire des bugs. Rien de tout cela n'a besoin d'un proxy ; cela a besoin d'une plateforme API. C'est là que la plupart des heures quotidiennes de Fiddler étaient réellement consacrées, et c'est pourquoi l'abonnement Everywhere pique : vous payez des prix de proxy pour du travail de client.

Si votre usage est principalement la Tâche 1, passez à la section des outils de capture. Si c'est principalement la Tâche 2, continuez à lire ; c'est le travail pour lequel Apidog a été conçu. (Pour le paysage plus large, voir outils de capture de paquets et Apidog.)

La réponse : Apidog

Apidog est une plateforme de développement API utilisée par plus de 500 000 développeurs : conception, débogage, test, simulation et documentation dans une seule application, pilotée par une seule spécification. Pour un ancien utilisateur de Fiddler, quatre choses comptent :

  1. Le Composer, adulte. Les Compose Requests de Fiddler construisent des appels ponctuels. Le client de requêtes d'Apidog couvre HTTP, WebSocket, SSE, gRPC et GraphQL, avec des environnements, des assistants d'authentification, des cookies, du scripting et de la génération de code — et chaque requête que vous enregistrez peut devenir un point de terminaison documenté avec un schéma, au lieu d'une ligne dans un journal de session.
  2. Les règles AutoResponder deviennent un serveur mock. C'est l'histoire de migration la plus solide, cartographiée concrètement ci-dessous. Au lieu d'une liste de règles locale faisant correspondre des URL et renvoyant des fichiers préenregistrés, le mock intelligent d'Apidog sert des réponses fausses conscientes du schéma depuis une URL réelle que toute votre équipe et la CI peuvent atteindre, sans aucune règle à écrire pour le cas par défaut.
  3. Le replay devient des tests de régression. Réémettre manuellement une session enregistrée se transforme en scénarios de test visuels : requêtes enchaînées, assertions, validation de schéma, exécutions pilotées par les données, lancées selon un calendrier ou en CI via l'Apidog CLI.
  4. Le prix est nul pour les petites équipes. Le plan gratuit couvre jusqu'à 4 utilisateurs, avec des exécutions illimitées, la simulation et des documents publiés. Les plans payants commencent à 9 $ par utilisateur et par mois, dans la même fourchette qu'un seul siège Fiddler Everywhere Pro.

À quoi ressemble le changement, fonctionnalité par fonctionnalité

Composer et inspecter des requêtes

Le travail quotidien sur les requêtes se traduit directement : construisez la requête, envoyez-la, inspectez le statut, les en-têtes, le corps et le timing. Apidog ajoute ce qu'une session proxy n'a jamais eu : des dossiers et des environnements au lieu d'un journal de capture, une validation de schéma pour qu'une charge utile erronée échoue bruyamment, et un historique que vous pouvez transformer en documentation. Ce que vous perdez, c'est la capture passive du trafic d'autres applications ; c'est la Tâche 1, et cela reste avec un proxy. Si votre habitude de capture était « regarder mon propre front-end appeler ma propre API », les DevTools du navigateur plus un client de requêtes est le chemin le plus léger — le même modèle que nous décrivons dans comment installer et utiliser Postman Interceptor.

Des règles AutoResponder aux mocks intelligents

Voici la cartographie concrète. Une configuration typique d'AutoResponder Fiddler pour le travail front-end :

EXACT:https://api.example.com~ (fichier local sur disque)

Puis une règle par point de terminaison, Fiddler à garder en cours d'exécution, et l'espoir que personne d'autre n'ait besoin du même backend factice sur sa machine.

Dans Apidog : définissez le point de terminaison GET ~, sans règle écrite. Besoin d'une charge utile fixe ? Attachezusers-42.json` comme exemple de réponse. Besoin que l'id 42 renvoie 200 et que l'id 99 renvoie 404 ? Ajoutez des attentes qui correspondent aux paramètres. Cela couvre chaque modèle AutoResponder (fichier statique, faux par point de terminaison, réponse conditionnelle) avec trois améliorations : le mock est partagé par URL au lieu d'être piégé dans le proxy d'une seule machine, il reste synchronisé avec la spécification, et il ne fait pas passer tout le trafic de votre système par un intercepteur juste pour simuler une API.

Tests, documentation et spécification

C'est un saut de catégorie plutôt qu'une traduction. Les sessions Fiddler meurent avec la fenêtre ; les points de terminaison Apidog s'accumulent dans une définition d'API qui génère des documents interactifs sur votre domaine, des mocks pour les consommateurs et des scénarios de test pour la CI. Si l'ensemble de comparaison réel de votre équipe est Postman ou Insomnia plutôt que Fiddler, nous avons fait ces face-à-face dans la meilleure alternative à Postman et la meilleure alternative à Insomnia.

Fiddler vs Apidog en un coup d'œil

Fiddler Classic Fiddler Everywhere Apidog
Prix Gratuit, non commercial uniquement 7 $/13 $/37 $ par utilisateur/mois (annuel) Gratuit jusqu'à 4 utilisateurs ; payant à partir de 9 $
Plateformes Windows uniquement Windows, macOS, Linux Windows, macOS, Linux, web
Statut Mode maintenance Actif Actif
Capture de trafic à l'échelle du système Oui Oui Non
Composer des requêtes API Composer de base Compose Requests Client complet : HTTP, WebSocket, SSE, gRPC, GraphQL
Simulation de réponse Règles AutoResponder, local Moteur de règles (niveau Pro), local Serveur mock intelligent conscient du schéma, URL partagée, gratuit
Points de terminaison enregistrés et documentés Non Sessions et requêtes enregistrées Points de terminaison basés sur une spécification avec documents publiés
Tests automatisés Non Basé sur le replay Scénarios visuels, assertions, pilotés par les données, CI
Exécutions CLI / CI Non Non Gratuit via Apidog CLI
Collaboration d'équipe Non Niveau Pro Plan gratuit, 4 utilisateurs

Le calcul des sièges, honnêtement

Une équipe de 5 personnes qui veut des règles de trafic et de la collaboration a besoin de Fiddler Everywhere Pro : 13 $ × 5 × 12 = 780 $ par an. La même équipe faisant du travail API dans Apidog paie 0 $ pour 4 sièges, plus 108 $ pour le cinquième à 9 $ par mois — soit 540 $ par an dans le scénario où tout le monde paie, toujours en dessous de la facture Fiddler. Mais le cadre plus juste est l'adéquation, pas le prix : ces sièges Fiddler achètent une capture de trafic dont le travail API n'a pas besoin, et n'achètent pas la spécification, la documentation, les mocks partagés ou les tests CI dont il a besoin. Payez des prix de proxy uniquement pour les personnes qui déboguent réellement du trafic étranger.

Pour une véritable capture de trafic, utilisez un outil de capture

Quand la tâche est l'interception MITM, choisissez un proxy ; ne forcez pas un client API dans ce rôle :

  • mitmproxy : gratuit, open source, multiplateforme ; console, interface web et scripting Python ; la réponse par défaut quand « remplacement gratuit de Fiddler » signifie la partie proxy.
  • Charles Proxy : licence payante unique ; choix de longue date pour le débogage d'applications mobiles, avec limitation et règles de réécriture. Il a ses propres questions d'outil vieillissant, que nous couvrons dans la meilleure alternative à Charles Proxy.
  • HTTP Toolkit : open core, interception en un clic de navigateurs, terminaux et conteneurs Docker spécifiques plutôt que du système entier ; la configuration la plus douce du groupe.
  • Proxyman : macOS natif (avec support des appareils iOS) ; le choix poli pour les équipes centrées Apple.

Un proxy de capture plus Apidog est une pile cohérente : le proxy pour la rare chasse au trafic étranger, Apidog pour le travail API quotidien. Pour démêler les proxys de débogage de l'autre type, voir Proxy API vs passerelle API expliqué.

Quand Fiddler a encore du sens

Fiddler Everywhere est le bon outil si la capture déchiffrée à l'échelle du système est votre travail quotidien et que vous voulez un produit commercial pris en charge derrière ; 13 $ par mois est raisonnable pour cela. Fiddler Classic reste défendable pour le débogage de loisir sur une machine Windows personnelle, licence et tout. Et les vétérans de FiddlerScript, avec des années de règles personnalisées, ont des coûts de changement qu'aucun bouton d'importation n'efface. Le passage à Apidog porte ses fruits dès que votre usage de Fiddler est principalement le Composer et AutoResponder : lorsque vous simulez votre propre backend via un proxy système, un serveur mock avec une URL est simplement la meilleure forme.

Questions fréquemment posées

Fiddler est-il encore gratuit ?

Fiddler Classic est gratuit mais restreint : usage non commercial uniquement, Windows uniquement, mode maintenance. Fiddler Everywhere n'a pas de niveau gratuit, seulement un essai de 10 jours, puis de 7 $ à 37 $ par utilisateur et par mois. Pour le travail API commercial sur un plan gratuit, voir le paysage des meilleures alternatives à Postman ou commencez avec le plan gratuit 4 utilisateurs d'Apidog.

Apidog peut-il capturer tout le trafic HTTP de mon système comme Fiddler ?

Non. Apidog est une plateforme de développement API, pas un proxy MITM à l'échelle du système, et nous ne prétendrons pas le contraire. Pour déchiffrer le trafic arbitraire d'applications ou mobiles, utilisez mitmproxy, Charles, HTTP Toolkit ou Proxyman ; notre guide des outils de capture de paquets les compare et montre où chacun s'intègre aux côtés d'Apidog.

Qu'est-ce qui remplace l'AutoResponder de Fiddler dans Apidog ?

Le serveur mock intelligent. Définissez ou importez un point de terminaison et Apidog sert immédiatement des réponses fausses basées sur un schéma à une URL mock partagée ; attachez des exemples pour des charges utiles fixes et des attentes pour des cas conditionnels. Contrairement aux règles AutoResponder, les mocks vivent avec la spécification et fonctionnent pour les coéquipiers et la CI sans que personne n'exécute un proxy, et ils s'exécutent dans votre pipeline via l'Apidog CLI.

Comment déplacer mon flux de travail Fiddler dans Apidog ?

Importez le fichier OpenAPI de votre API pour que chaque point de terminaison arrive avec schémas, documents et mocks en direct en une fois, puis portez les règles AutoResponder comme exemples de réponse et attentes. Les archives de session SAZ de Fiddler ne sont pas un format de collection : traitez donc le déménagement comme l'importation de votre spécification, pas de votre historique de capture.

Fiddler Everywhere est-il identique à Fiddler Classic ?

Non. Everywhere est un produit d'abonnement multiplateforme réécrit ; Classic est le freeware Windows figé, et Telerik oriente les utilisateurs commerciaux vers Everywhere. Pour la même bifurcation dans l'outil voisin, voir la meilleure alternative à Charles Proxy.

Arrêtez de payer des prix de proxy pour le travail API

Si Fiddler était votre composeur de requêtes et votre faux backend, déplacez ce travail vers l'outil conçu pour cela. Importez votre spécification OpenAPI, obtenez des points de terminaison documentés avec des mocks intelligents en direct en quelques minutes, et câblez les tests dans la CI. Téléchargez Apidog ou commencez dans le navigateur ; une équipe de 4 ne paie rien, et les règles AutoResponder que vous avez surveillées deviennent des URL mock que vous pouvez partager.

title: Why Does Python Fail to Verify SSL Certificates? Common Causes and Practical Fixes
description:
Have you ever run a Python script that works perfectly on your local machine but fails when it tries to connect to an HTTPS API?

You might see an error similar to this:

requests.exceptions.SSLError:
HTTPSConnectionPool(host='example.com', port=443):
Max retries exceeded with url: /
(Caused by SSLError(
SSLCertVerificationError:
certificate verify failed
))

This error can be frustrating, especially when the website opens normally in your browser.

But why does Python reject an SSL certificate that your browser appears to trust?

The answer usually comes down to how Python verifies certificate chains and which Certificate Authorities (CAs) its environment trusts.

Let's look at the common causes and how to troubleshoot them.

1. Why Does Python Reject an SSL Certificate?

When Python connects to an HTTPS website, it checks the server's TLS certificate to establish that it is connecting to the intended server and that the certificate chains back to a trusted CA.

Several things can cause this verification to fail:

The certificate has expired.

The server isn't providing the complete certificate chain.

The local CA certificate bundle is outdated.

The certificate was issued by a private or untrusted CA.

A corporate proxy is intercepting HTTPS connections.

The application is using an incorrect or incomplete CA bundle.

The important thing to understand is that a browser and a Python application may use different certificate trust stores.

Therefore, a website working in Chrome doesn't necessarily mean that a Python script will trust its certificate.

2. Check Whether the Problem Is With Python or the Server

Before changing your Python configuration, check the certificate presented by the server.

You can use OpenSSL:

openssl s_client -connect example.com:443 -servername example.com -showcerts

Replace example.com with the hostname you're trying to access.

Look for the verification result near the bottom of the output.

For example:

Verify return code: 0 (ok)

This indicates that OpenSSL successfully verified the certificate chain using its configured trust store.

If you see a verification error, investigate the certificate chain, hostname, expiry, and trusted CA configuration.

Note: OpenSSL and Python may use different CA bundles, so a successful OpenSSL check doesn't automatically prove that Python will succeed.

3. Update Python's Certificate Bundle

One common cause is an outdated CA certificate bundle.

The Python requests library uses trusted CA certificates to verify HTTPS connections. It commonly uses the certifi package to provide a CA bundle.

First, update the relevant packages:

python -m pip install --upgrade requests certifi

Next, check which CA bundle certifi is using:

import certifi

print(certifi.where())

This prints the path to the CA certificate bundle.

You can also explicitly tell Requests to use it:

import requests
import certifi

response = requests.get(
"https://example.com",
verify=certifi.where(),
timeout=15
)

print(response.status_code)

If the request succeeds, the issue may have been related to the previous CA bundle configuration.

4. Check Whether Your Server Is Sending the Complete Certificate Chain

Another common problem occurs when a web server doesn't provide the required intermediate certificates.

A TLS certificate chain generally contains:

The server certificate.

One or more intermediate CA certificates.

A trusted root CA certificate, which is generally already present in the client's trust store.

If the server fails to provide a required intermediate certificate, some clients may be unable to build a trusted chain.

You can inspect the certificate chain using:

openssl s_client \
-connect example.com:443 \
-servername example.com \
-showcerts \
-verify_return_error

Check whether the expected intermediate certificates are being presented and whether chain verification succeeds.

If the chain is incomplete, correct the server's certificate-chain configuration rather than disabling verification in Python.

5. Configure a Custom CA Bundle When Necessary

Sometimes the problem isn't an outdated public CA bundle.

For example, your organization might use:

An internal Certificate Authority.

A private PKI environment.

A corporate HTTPS inspection proxy.

Custom certificates for internal APIs.

In these situations, Python may need to trust an additional CA certificate.

Requests supports specifying a custom CA bundle through the verify parameter:

import requests

response = requests.get(
"https://internal.example.com",
verify="/path/to/company-ca-bundle.pem",
timeout=15
)

print(response.status_code)

You can also configure the REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE environment variable:

Linux/macOS:

export REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE=/path/to/company-ca-bundle.pem

Windows PowerShell:

$env:REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE = "C:\certs\company-ca-bundle.pem"

Make sure the file contains the appropriate trusted CA certificates and is maintained securely.

If you need both public and private CA trust, use a properly constructed combined CA bundle rather than accidentally replacing public trust with an incomplete private bundle.

6. Check for HTTPS Inspection by a Corporate Proxy

If your Python application works on your home network but fails on an office network, check whether a corporate proxy is inspecting HTTPS traffic.

Some organizations intercept encrypted connections and issue replacement certificates signed by an internal CA.

Your browser may already trust that internal CA because it was installed through your organization's device-management policy.

Python may not automatically use the same trust configuration.

To investigate:

Compare the certificate issuer on your office and home networks.

Check whether your organization uses HTTPS inspection.

Ask your IT administrator for the approved CA certificate bundle.

Configure your Python application to trust the appropriate CA.

Never install an unknown CA certificate simply to make an SSL error disappear. Verify its authenticity with your IT or security team.

7. Why You Shouldn't Disable SSL Verification

You may find examples online that suggest using:

requests.get(
"https://example.com",
verify=False
)

This disables certificate verification for that request.

Although it might make the connection work, it also removes an important security check. Your application could accept an untrusted or impersonated server certificate.

This increases the risk of man-in-the-middle attacks.

Instead of disabling verification, identify why the certificate cannot be trusted and fix the underlying problem.

A Quick Troubleshooting Checklist

If your Python application still cannot verify an SSL certificate, work through this checklist:

Check whether the server certificate has expired.

Verify that the hostname matches the certificate.

Check whether the server sends the required intermediate certificates.

Update Requests and Certifi.

Check which CA bundle your application uses.

Investigate corporate proxies or private CAs.

Test the connection again without disabling certificate verification.

Final Thoughts

Python SSL certificate verification errors aren't always caused by an invalid website certificate. Sometimes the issue is with the local CA bundle, missing intermediate certificates, or a network environment that uses its own trusted CA.

The best approach is to identify where certificate verification fails before changing your application's security settings.

If you regularly work with APIs, backend services, or automated deployments, keeping CA bundles updated and monitoring certificate chains can help prevent unexpected connection failures.

Have you encountered an SSL certificate verification error in Python? Was it caused by an outdated CA bundle, a missing intermediate certificate, or something else? Share your experience in the comments.

title: Gemini API CLI: ให้ Coding Agent ของคุณเรียกใช้ Gemini สำหรับรูปภาพ วิดีโอ PDF และ Deep Research
description:
Gemini API CLI (gemini-api) คือไคลเอนต์บรรทัดคำสั่งโอเพนซอร์สของ Google สำหรับ Gemini API สร้างขึ้นเพื่อเอเจนต์เขียนโค้ดอย่าง Claude Code, Codex, Cursor และ Antigravity ติดตั้งไบนารี Go เพียงตัวเดียว ตั้งค่า GEMINI_API_KEY แล้วเอเจนต์ของคุณก็สร้างรูปภาพ วิดีโอ เสียงพูด และเพลง วิเคราะห์ไฟล์ PDF และไฟล์บันทึกเสียง ถอดเสียงเป็น SRT และเริ่ม Deep Research แบบเบื้องหลังได้

ลองใช้ Apidog วันนี้

ด้านล่างนี้: การติดตั้ง การยืนยันตัวตน คำสั่งที่เอเจนต์ของคุณจะรัน ความแตกต่างจาก Gemini CLI และวิธีจับคู่กับ Apidog CLI ทุกแฟล็กคัดลอกจาก gemini-api --help ในเวอร์ชัน 0.4.5 ซึ่งเผยแพร่เมื่อวันที่ 30 ตุลาคม 2026

Gemini API CLI คืออะไร?

Gemini API CLI เป็นไคลเอนต์แบบไม่เก็บสถานะ (stateless) ในรูปแบบไบนารีเดียวสำหรับ Interactions API ของ Google แต่ละคำสั่งคือการเรียก HTTP หนึ่งครั้ง: ส่งพรอมป์ต์เข้าไป แล้วได้เส้นทางไฟล์ ข้อความถอดเสียง ผลวิเคราะห์ หรือ ID ของ interaction ออกมา — เป็นเครื่องมือที่เอเจนต์ที่มีอยู่แล้วของคุณเรียกใช้เมื่อเจองานที่ต้องใช้ Gemini

หน้าเอกสารอย่างเป็นทางการของ Google เรียกมันว่า "รีลีสเบต้าโอเพนซอร์สที่พัฒนาควบคู่ไปกับ Interactions API" โค้ดอยู่ที่ google-gemini/gemini-api-cli ภายใต้สัญญาอนุญาต Apache 2.0 และทำงานบน macOS, Linux และ Windows

นี่คือสิ่งที่ gemini-api --help แสดงในเวอร์ชัน 0.4.5 พร้อมโมเดลเริ่มต้นของแต่ละคำสั่ง:

กลุ่ม คำสั่ง หน้าที่ โมเดลเริ่มต้น
Create generate สร้างข้อความและมัลติโหมด gemini-3.8-flash
Create image สร้างหรือแก้ไขรูปภาพ gemini-nano-banana-2.1
Create video สร้างและแก้ไขวิดีโอ gemini-omni-1.1-flash
Create tts / music เสียงพูดและเพลง gemini-3.8-flash-tts / lyria-3.5
Understand analyze ถามคำถามเกี่ยวกับ PDF รูปภาพ เสียง วิดีโอ และ URL ของ YouTube gemini-3.8-flash
Understand transcribe แปลงเสียงหรือวิดีโอเป็น md, text, json หรือ srt gemini-3.5-transcribe
Manage agent รันโมเดลหรือ managed agent เช่น Deep Research กำหนดต่อการรันแต่ละครั้ง
Manage files อัปโหลดผ่าน Files API เก็บไว้ 48 ชั่วโมง ไม่มี

Gemini API CLI กับ Gemini CLI

ชื่อใกล้กันมาก นี่คือความแตกต่าง Gemini CLI (@google/gemini-cli) เป็นเอเจนต์เขียนโค้ดแบบอินเทอร์แอกทีฟ ซึ่งเป็นทางเลือกแทน Claude Code ที่คุณสนทนาด้วย ส่วน Gemini API CLI (gemini-api) ไม่มีลูปเอเจนต์เลย มันเป็นเครื่องมือที่เอเจนต์ตัวอื่นเป็นคนรัน

Gemini API CLI Gemini CLI
ไบนารี gemini-api gemini
บทบาท เครื่องมือที่เอเจนต์ของคุณเรียกใช้ เอเจนต์ที่คุณพูดคุยด้วย
เอาต์พุตสื่อ รูปภาพ วิดีโอ เสียงพูด เพลง ลงดิสก์ ไม่ใช่จุดเน้นของมัน
เหมาะที่สุดสำหรับ มอบโมเดลของ Gemini ให้ Claude Code, Codex หรือ Cursor การใช้ Gemini เป็นเอเจนต์เขียนโค้ดของคุณ

หากคุณทำงานใน Claude Code หรือ Codex และต้องการใช้โมเดลด้านสื่อและงานวิจัยของ Gemini ภายในเวิร์กโฟลว์นั้น ให้ใช้ gemini-api ในรูปแบบเดียวกับ OpenAI CLI เพียงแต่ชี้ไปที่ Google

วิธีติดตั้ง Gemini API CLI

เลือกหนึ่งในสี่วิธีจาก README

macOS และ Linux:

curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/google-gemini/gemini-api-cli/main/scripts/install.sh | bash

Windows (PowerShell):

iwr -useb https://raw.githubusercontent.com/google-gemini/gemini-api-cli/main/scripts/install.ps1 | iex

Go:

go install github.com/google-gemini/gemini-api-cli/cmd/gemini-api@latest

ไบนารีที่คอมไพล์ไว้แล้ว: ดาวน์โหลดไฟล์เก็บถาวรสำหรับแพลตฟอร์มของคุณจาก GitHub Releases ตรวจสอบกับ checksums.txt แล้ววาง gemini-api ไว้ใน PATH ของคุณ เราใช้ไฟล์เก็บถาวร Darwin_arm64 โดย shasum -a 256 -c checksums.txt --ignore-missing แสดงผลเป็น OK

Google เตือนว่าการเปลี่ยนแปลงที่ทำให้ของเดิมพังอาจเกิดขึ้นได้ระหว่างเวอร์ชันไมเนอร์ ดังนั้นควรปักหมุดรีลีสใน CI เอกสารแสดงสคริปต์ติดตั้งโดยวาง GEMINI_VERSION=<release-tag> ไว้ข้างหน้า bash

ตรวจสอบการติดตั้ง:

gemini-api version
# gemini-api 0.4.5

การยืนยันตัวตนของ Gemini API CLI

สร้างคีย์ใน Google AI Studio (คู่มือวิธีขอ Gemini API key ฟรีของเราอธิบายขั้นตอนไว้ทั้งหมด) จากนั้น export คีย์:

export GEMINI_API_KEY="YOUR_API_KEY"

บนเครื่องของคุณเอง เก็บคีย์ไว้แทนได้:

gemini-api configure --api-key "YOUR_API_KEY"
gemini-api whoami

configure จะบันทึกคีย์ลงใน keychain ของระบบปฏิบัติการของคุณ (macOS Keychain, Linux Secret Service หรือ Windows Credential Manager) เพิ่มแฟล็กโกลบอล --no-keyring หากต้องการเก็บไว้ใน ~/.config/gemini-api/config.yaml แทน ส่วน whoami จะแสดงว่าขณะนี้ใช้ข้อมูลรับรองตัวใดและมาจากไหน

เมื่อยังไม่ได้ตั้งค่าคีย์ gemini-api --help จะแสดงข้อความที่ส่งถึงตัวเอเจนต์เองว่า API key "ต้องถูกสร้างด้วยมือโดยผู้ใช้ใน Google AI Studio ให้หยุดและขอให้ผู้ใช้สร้างขึ้นมา" เอเจนต์ของคุณจะถามคุณแทนที่จะตั้งค่าคีย์ด้วยตัวเอง

ดูตัวอย่างทุกการเรียกด้วย --dry-run

--dry-run จะตรวจสอบแฟล็กและแสดงคำขอโดยปิดบังข้อมูลรับรอง โดยไม่มีการเรียกผ่านเครือข่ายและไม่มีการอ่าน keychain ใช้งานได้ก่อนที่คุณจะตั้งค่าคีย์ ซึ่งเป็นวิธีที่เราใช้ตรวจสอบทุกตัวอย่างในบทความนี้

นี่คือตัวอย่าง dry run จริงของงาน Deep Research ที่รันเบื้องหลัง:

ทุกคำสั่งจะ POST ไปที่ https://generativelanguage.googleapis.com/v1beta/interactions เพิ่ม -o json เพื่อให้ได้ JSON หนึ่งออบเจ็กต์ต่อหนึ่งคำขอทาง stdout ซึ่งเอเจนต์สามารถแยกวิเคราะห์ได้ก่อนที่จะใช้โทเคน

คำสั่ง Gemini API CLI ที่เอเจนต์ของคุณจะรัน

สร้างและแก้ไขรูปภาพ 

gemini-api image "A friendly robot mascot, soft studio lighting" --out ./assets/mascot.jpg
gemini-api image "Add a winter scarf" -i ./assets/mascot.jpg --out ./assets/mascot-winter.jpg

คำสั่งเกี่ยวกับสื่อจะเขียนไฟล์และแสดงเพียงเส้นทางของไฟล์ ดังนั้นเอเจนต์จะจับค่านั้นด้วย $(...) แล้วทำงานต่อไปได้ image ยังรองรับ --aspect-ratio และ --image-size (512, 1K, 2K หรือ 4K) โมเดลเริ่มต้นคือ Nano Banana 2.1 ดูคู่มือ Nano Banana 2.1 APIของเราเพื่อรู้ว่ามันทำอะไรได้ดี

สร้างวิดีโอ เสียงพูด และเพลง 

gemini-api video "A slow camera move through a sunlit workshop" --resolution 1080p --out ./assets/
gemini-api tts "Welcome. Let's build something together." --out ./assets/welcome.wav
gemini-api music "Warm ambient music for a product walkthrough" --out ./assets/

วิดีโอใช้เวลานานกว่า ดังนั้น video จะ polling ให้คุณ ใช้ --async เพื่อรับ operation handle ทันที และ --resume <id> เพื่อกลับมา polling ต่อในภายหลัง --resolution มีค่าเริ่มต้นเป็น 720p

วิเคราะห์ PDF รูปภาพ และ URL ของ YouTube 

gemini-api analyze -i product-brief.pdf "What should we build first, and why?" > plan.md
gemini-api analyze -i before.png -i after.png "Summarize the visual design changes"

-i/--input ใช้ซ้ำได้และรองรับเส้นทางไฟล์ในเครื่อง, URI แบบ files/<id> หรือ URL ของ YouTube อินพุตแบบอินไลน์จำกัดที่ประมาณ 14 MB (ขนาดดิบ) สำหรับไฟล์ที่ใหญ่กว่า ให้อัปโหลดครั้งเดียวแล้วนำ URI กลับมาใช้ซ้ำ:

FILE_URI=$(gemini-api files upload interview.mp4 --wait --output-format json --jq '.name')
gemini-api analyze -i "$FILE_URI" "List the key action items with timestamps"

ไฟล์ที่อัปโหลดจะถูกลบหลัง 48 ชั่วโมง

ถอดเสียงจากไฟล์เสียงและวิดีโอ 

gemini-api transcribe -i interview.mp4 --format srt --out interview.srt

--format รับค่า md (ค่าเริ่มต้น), text, json หรือ srt เพิ่ม --no-speakers หรือ --no-timestamps เพื่อตัดผู้พูดหรือเวลาออกจากเอาต์พุต

รัน Deep Research ในเบื้องหลัง 

ID=$(gemini-api agent run "Research battery recycling approaches and cite sources" \
  --agent deep-research-preview-04-2026 --background --jq '.id')
gemini-api agent status "$ID" --stream=false --output-format json

--background จะคืนค่า interaction ID ทันทีแทนที่จะเปิดสตรีมค้างไว้ เอเจนต์จะเก็บ ID นั้นไว้ ไปทำงานอย่างอื่น แล้วกลับมาตรวจสอบด้วย agent status ส่วน agent cancel ใช้หยุดการรัน ผลลัพธ์ help ของ 0.4.5 ยังระบุ deep-research-max-preview-04-2026 และ antigravity-preview-05-2026 เป็น managed agent ด้วย

แฟล็กที่ทำให้ gemini-api ปลอดภัยสำหรับเอเจนต์

นี่คือแฟล็กโกลบอลที่ควรใส่ไว้ในคำสั่งของเอเจนต์คุณ ทั้งหมดมาจาก gemini-api --help-global:

  • --agent-mode (หรือ GEMINI_CLI_AGENT_MODE=1): ข้อผิดพลาดแบบ JSON ที่มีโครงสร้างทาง stderr และเอาต์พุต TOON แบบกะทัดรัดทาง stdout
  • -o, --output-format: pretty, json, yaml, table หรือ toon
  • -q, --jq: กรองเอาต์พุตแบบอินไลน์ เช่น --jq '.id'
  • --no-interactive: ไม่มีพรอมป์ต์หรือฟอร์ม TUI ซึ่งเป็นสิ่งที่เอเจนต์แบบไม่มีหน้าจอ (headless) ต้องการ
  • --usage: โครงสร้างคำสั่งทั้งหมดในรูปแบบ KDL ที่เครื่องอ่านได้
  • --schema (ต่อคำสั่ง): JSON Schema สำหรับเพย์โหลด --body

รหัสออก (exit code) บอกเอเจนต์ว่าเกิดอะไรขึ้นโดยไม่ต้องแยกวิเคราะห์ข้อความ: 0 สำเร็จ, 1 ข้อผิดพลาดขณะรันหรือจาก API, 2 ข้อผิดพลาดในการใช้งานหรือการตรวจสอบความถูกต้อง, 3 การยืนยันตัวตน ข้อควรระวังอย่างหนึ่ง: คำสั่งแบบสตรีมมิ่ง (generate, agent run) ต้องใช้ --stream=false ก่อน -o json หรือ --jq จึงจะให้ผลลัพธ์เดียวที่แยกวิเคราะห์ได้

มอบ Gemini API CLI ให้เอเจนต์เขียนโค้ดของคุณ

README ของ Google มีบล็อกให้คัดลอกไปวางใน AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md หรือ .cursorrules (ตัดมาเฉพาะบางส่วน):

You have access to gemini-api through the shell.
1. Inspect --help or --usage to choose a command, and --schema when building a --body JSON payload.
2. Preview API calls with --dry-run.
3. For JSON output or --jq on streaming commands, pass --stream=false --output-format json.
4. Capture returned file paths and interaction IDs to continue multi-step tasks.

ตรวจสอบให้แน่ใจว่า GEMINI_API_KEY ไปถึงสภาพแวดล้อมของโปรเซสย่อยของเอเจนต์ จากนั้นสั่งงานตามปกติ: "สร้างแลนดิ้งเพจ ใช้ Gemini ทำรูปมาสคอตและเสียงบรรยาย 20 วินาที และเริ่มรัน Deep Research เกี่ยวกับผลิตภัณฑ์คู่แข่ง" เอเจนต์จะเป็นคนเลือกคำสั่งเอง

สิ่งที่มันทำไม่ได้: เสียงหรือวิดีโอแบบเรียลไทม์ ไม่มีการรองรับ WebSocket ดังนั้น Live API จึงยังต้องใช้ GenAI SDK

ทดสอบ API ที่คุณสร้างด้วย Apidog CLI

gemini-api มอบโมเดลของ Gemini ให้เอเจนต์ของคุณ แต่มันไม่รู้อะไรเลยเกี่ยวกับ API ของคุณเอง ไม่ว่าจะเป็น endpoint /summarize หรือ /thumbnail ที่แอปของคุณห่อไว้รอบ Gemini สภาพแวดล้อมต่างๆ ของมัน หรือ assertion ที่พิสูจน์ได้ว่ารีลีสใหม่ไม่ได้ทำให้อะไรพัง นั่นคืองานของ Apidog CLI และเอเจนต์ตัวเดียวกันก็รันทั้งสองอย่างได้

ตั้งค่าเพียงครั้งเดียว:

npm install -g apidog-cli@latest
apidog login --with-token <YOUR_TOKEN>
npx -y skills add https://apidog.com   # pick your agent when prompted

จากนั้นสั่งเอเจนต์ด้วยพรอมป์ต์เดียว:

Use gemini-api to dry-run an analyze call on ./docs/sample-invoice.pdf, then run it for real.
Import ./openapi.yaml into Apidog project <id>, create a test case for POST /v1/invoices/extract
that uploads the same PDF and asserts a 200 and a non-empty "total" field, run it against the
staging environment, and summarize any failures.

เอเจนต์จะตรวจสอบคำตอบของ Gemini ด้วย gemini-api จากนั้นอ่าน schema ของ Apidog ก่อนเขียนเพย์โหลด ตรวจสอบความถูกต้อง และสร้างและรันเทสต์เคส:

apidog import --project <id> --format openapi --file ./openapi.yaml
apidog cli-schema get test-case-create
apidog cli-schema validate test-case-create --file case.json
apidog test-case create --project <id> --file case.json
apidog run --test-case <caseId> --project <id> -e <envId> -r cli,json

apidog test-case create --help เตือนถึงกับดักอย่างหนึ่ง: เทสต์เคสต้องมี categoryId ที่ถูกต้อง ดังนั้นให้ลิสต์รายการก่อนด้วย apidog test-case category --project <id> เปลี่ยน -r cli,json เป็น -r junit แล้วบรรทัดเดิมก็รันใน CI ได้ หากคุณใช้ Claude Code เป็นเอเจนต์ เริ่มจาก Apidog CLI ใน Claude Code แพลนฟรีของ Apidog รองรับผู้ใช้สูงสุด 4 คน

คำถามที่พบบ่อย

Gemini API CLI ใช้ฟรีหรือไม่? ตัว CLI เองฟรีและเป็นโอเพนซอร์สภายใต้ Apache 2.0 ทุกการเรียกจะคิดเงินกับ API key ของคุณตามราคา Gemini APIปกติ สำหรับรายละเอียดว่าแพ็กเกจฟรีครอบคลุมอะไรบ้าง ดูคู่มือ Gemini API free tierของเรา

gemini-api เหมือนกับ Gemini CLI ไหม? ไม่เหมือน Gemini CLI เป็นเอเจนต์เขียนโค้ดแบบอินเทอร์แอกทีฟ ส่วน gemini-api เป็นเครื่องมือแบบไม่เก็บสถานะที่เอเจนต์ตัวอื่น สคริปต์ และงานใน CI เรียกใช้เพื่อเข้าถึงโมเดลของ Gemini และ managed agent

ทดสอบคำสั่งโดยไม่มี API key ได้ไหม? ได้ --dry-run จะตรวจสอบคำสั่งและแสดงคำขอแบบตรงทั้งหมดโดยไม่มีการเรียกผ่านเครือข่ายและไม่มีการอ่าน keychain ทุกตัวอย่างในบทความนี้ตรวจสอบด้วยวิธีนั้นบนเวอร์ชัน 0.4.5

จะจัดการไฟล์ที่ใหญ่กว่า 14 MB อย่างไร? รัน gemini-api files upload <file> --wait เก็บค่า files/<id> ที่ได้ และส่งค่านั้นให้ -i ใน analyze, transcribe, generate, image, video หรือ agent run ไฟล์ที่อัปโหลดจะหมดอายุหลัง 48 ชั่วโมง

ควรปักหมุดเวอร์ชันไหม? ควร โดยเฉพาะใน CI Google ระบุว่าการเปลี่ยนแปลงที่ทำให้ของเดิมพังอาจเกิดขึ้นได้ระหว่างเวอร์ชันไมเนอร์ในขณะที่ CLI ยังอยู่ในช่วงเบต้า

title: Gemini API CLI: 코딩 에이전트가 이미지, 동영상, PDF, Deep Research를 위해 Gemini를 호출하도록 하기
description:
Gemini API CLI: 코딩 에이전트가 이미지, 동영상, PDF, Deep Research를 위해 Gemini를 호출하도록 하기

Gemini API CLI(gemini-api)는 Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Antigravity 같은 코딩 에이전트를 위해 만들어진 Google의 오픈소스 Gemini API 명령줄 클라이언트입니다. Go 바이너리 하나를 설치하고 GEMINI_API_KEY를 설정하면, 에이전트가 이미지, 비디오, 음성, 음악을 생성하고, PDF와 녹음을 분석하며, 오디오를 SRT로 전사하고, 백그라운드에서 Deep Research를 실행할 수 있습니다.

지금 Apidog를 사용해 보세요

이 글은 설치, 인증, 에이전트가 실행할 명령, Gemini CLI와의 차이점, 그리고 Apidog CLI와 함께 사용하는 방법을 다룹니다. 모든 플래그는 2026년 10월 30일에 릴리스된 버전 0.4.5의 gemini-api --help에서 그대로 가져왔습니다.

Gemini API CLI란 무엇인가?

Gemini API CLI는 Google의 Interactions API를 위한 상태 비저장(stateless) 단일 바이너리 클라이언트입니다. 각 명령은 하나의 HTTP 호출입니다. 프롬프트가 들어가면 파일 경로, 전사본, 분석 결과 또는 인터랙션 ID가 나옵니다. 작업에 Gemini가 필요할 때 기존 에이전트가 호출하는 도구입니다.

Google의 공식 문서 페이지는 이를 "Interactions API와 함께 발전하는 오픈소스 베타 릴리스"라고 부릅니다. 코드는 Apache 2.0 라이선스로 google-gemini/gemini-api-cli에 있으며, macOS, Linux, Windows에서 실행됩니다.

다음은 0.4.5에서 gemini-api --help가 나열하는 내용과 각 명령의 기본 모델입니다:

그룹 명령 기능 기본 모델
Create generate 텍스트 및 멀티모달 생성 gemini-3.8-flash
Create image 이미지 생성 또는 편집 gemini-nano-banana-2.1
Create video 비디오 생성 및 편집 gemini-omni-1.1-flash
Create tts / music 음성 및 음악 gemini-3.8-flash-tts / lyria-3.5
Understand analyze PDF, 이미지, 오디오, 비디오, YouTube URL에 대한 질문 gemini-3.8-flash
Understand transcribe 오디오 또는 비디오를 md, text, json 또는 srt로 변환 gemini-3.5-transcribe
Manage agent 모델 또는 Deep Research 같은 관리형 에이전트 실행 실행별로 설정
Manage files Files API 업로드, 48시간 보존 해당 없음

Gemini API CLI vs Gemini CLI

이름이 비슷하니 차이를 정리하겠습니다. Gemini CLI(@google/gemini-cli)는 대화형 코딩 에이전트로, 당신이 대화하는 Claude Code 대안입니다. Gemini API CLI(gemini-api)에는 에이전트 루프가 전혀 없습니다. 다른 에이전트가 실행하는 도구입니다.

Gemini API CLI Gemini CLI
바이너리 gemini-api gemini
역할 에이전트가 호출하는 도구 당신이 대화하는 에이전트
미디어 출력 이미지, 비디오, 음성, 음악을 디스크에 저장 주요 초점 아님
최적 용도 Claude Code, Codex, Cursor에 Gemini 모델 제공 Gemini를 코딩 에이전트로 사용

Claude Code나 Codex에서 작업하며 그 워크플로 안에서 Gemini의 미디어 및 리서치 모델을 원한다면 gemini-api를 사용하세요. Google을 향해 있다는 점만 다를 뿐, OpenAI CLI와 동일한 패턴입니다.

Gemini API CLI 설치 방법

README에 있는 네 가지 방법 중 하나를 선택하세요.

macOS 및 Linux:

curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/google-gemini/gemini-api-cli/main/scripts/install.sh | bash

Windows (PowerShell):

iwr -useb https://raw.githubusercontent.com/google-gemini/gemini-api-cli/main/scripts/install.ps1 | iex

Go:

go install github.com/google-gemini/gemini-api-cli/cmd/gemini-api@latest

사전 빌드된 바이너리: GitHub Releases에서 자신의 플랫폼용 아카이브를 다운로드하고, checksums.txt와 대조한 뒤, gemini-api를 PATH에 넣으세요. 저희는 Darwin_arm64 아카이브를 사용했으며, shasum -a 256 -c checksums.txt --ignore-missing이 OK를 출력했습니다.

Google은 마이너 버전 간에 호환성을 깨는 변경이 발생할 수 있다고 경고하므로, CI에서는 릴리스를 고정(pin)하세요. 문서에서는 설치 스크립트에서 bash 앞에 GEMINI_VERSION=<release-tag>를 두는 방법을 보여줍니다.

설치를 확인하세요:

gemini-api version
# gemini-api 0.4.5

Gemini API CLI 인증

Google AI Studio에서 키를 생성한 다음(무료로 Gemini API 키 받기 가이드에서 자세히 다룹니다), 내보내세요:

export GEMINI_API_KEY="YOUR_API_KEY"

자신의 워크스테이션에서는 대신 저장할 수도 있습니다:

gemini-api configure --api-key "YOUR_API_KEY"
gemini-api whoami

configure는 키를 OS 키체인(macOS Keychain, Linux Secret Service 또는 Windows Credential Manager)에 저장합니다. 대신 ~/.config/gemini-api/config.yaml에 보관하려면 전역 --no-keyring 플래그를 추가하세요. whoami는 어떤 자격 증명이 활성 상태인지, 어디에서 왔는지 보여줍니다.

키가 설정되지 않은 경우, gemini-api --help는 에이전트 자체를 향한 문장을 출력합니다. API 키는 "사용자가 Google AI Studio에서 수동으로 생성해야 합니다. 중단하고 사용자에게 생성을 요청하세요."라고 나옵니다. 에이전트는 스스로 키를 구성하지 않고 당신에게 요청할 것입니다.

--dry-run으로 모든 호출 미리보기

--dry-run은 플래그를 검증하고 자격 증명을 가린 상태로 요청을 출력하며, 네트워크 호출도 키체인 읽기도 하지 않습니다. 키를 설정하기 전에도 작동하므로, 여기 있는 모든 예제를 이 방식으로 확인했습니다.

다음은 백그라운드 Deep Research 작업의 실제 dry run입니다:

모든 명령은 https://generativelanguage.googleapis.com/v1beta/interactions로 POST합니다. -o json을 추가하면 요청당 하나의 JSON 객체를 stdout으로 받을 수 있어, 에이전트가 토큰을 소비하기 전에 파싱할 수 있습니다.

에이전트가 실행할 Gemini API CLI 명령

이미지 생성 및 편집 

gemini-api image "A friendly robot mascot, soft studio lighting" --out ./assets/mascot.jpg
gemini-api image "Add a winter scarf" -i ./assets/mascot.jpg --out ./assets/mascot-winter.jpg

미디어 명령은 파일을 쓰고 해당 경로만 출력하므로, 에이전트는 $(...)로 이를 캡처하여 계속 작업을 이어갑니다. image는 --aspect-ratio와 --image-size(512, 1K, 2K 또는 4K)도 받습니다. 기본 모델은 Nano Banana 2.1이며, 이 모델이 잘하는 것은 Nano Banana 2.1 API 가이드를 참고하세요.

비디오, 음성, 음악 생성 

gemini-api video "A slow camera move through a sunlit workshop" --resolution 1080p --out ./assets/
gemini-api tts "Welcome. Let's build something together." --out ./assets/welcome.wav
gemini-api music "Warm ambient music for a product walkthrough" --out ./assets/

비디오는 더 오래 걸리므로 video가 대신 폴링합니다. --async를 사용하면 작업 핸들을 즉시 받고, --resume <id>로 나중에 폴링을 다시 시작할 수 있습니다. --resolution의 기본값은 720p입니다.

PDF, 이미지, YouTube URL 분석 

gemini-api analyze -i product-brief.pdf "What should we build first, and why?" > plan.md
gemini-api analyze -i before.png -i after.png "Summarize the visual design changes"

-i/--input은 반복 지정할 수 있으며, 로컬 경로, files/<id> URI, 또는 YouTube URL을 받습니다. 인라인 입력은 원본 기준 약 14MB로 제한됩니다. 더 큰 파일의 경우 한 번 업로드하고 URI를 재사용하세요:

FILE_URI=$(gemini-api files upload interview.mp4 --wait --output-format json --jq '.name')
gemini-api analyze -i "$FILE_URI" "List the key action items with timestamps"

업로드된 파일은 48시간 후에 삭제됩니다.

오디오 및 비디오 전사 

gemini-api transcribe -i interview.mp4 --format srt --out interview.srt

--format은 md(기본값), text, json 또는 srt를 받습니다. --no-speakers 또는 --no-timestamps를 추가하면 출력에서 화자나 타임스탬프를 제거할 수 있습니다.

백그라운드에서 Deep Research 실행 

ID=$(gemini-api agent run "Research battery recycling approaches and cite sources" \
  --agent deep-research-preview-04-2026 --background --jq '.id')
gemini-api agent status "$ID" --stream=false --output-format json

--background는 스트림을 열어둔 채 유지하는 대신 인터랙션 ID를 즉시 반환합니다. 에이전트는 ID를 저장하고 다른 작업을 하다가 agent status로 다시 확인합니다. agent cancel은 실행을 중지합니다. 0.4.5 도움말에는 deep-research-max-preview-04-2026과 antigravity-preview-05-2026도 관리형 에이전트로 나열되어 있습니다.

gemini-api를 에이전트에 안전하게 만드는 플래그

다음은 에이전트 지침에 넣을 만한 전역 플래그로, 모두 gemini-api --help-global에서 가져온 것입니다:

  • --agent-mode(또는 GEMINI_CLI_AGENT_MODE=1): stderr에 구조화된 JSON 오류, stdout에 간결한 TOON 출력.
  • -o, --output-format: pretty, json, yaml, table 또는 toon.
  • -q, --jq: 출력을 인라인으로 필터링합니다. 예를 들어 --jq '.id'.
  • --no-interactive: 프롬프트나 TUI 양식이 없으며, 헤드리스 에이전트에 필요합니다.
  • --usage: 전체 명령 트리를 기계 판독 가능한 KDL로 출력.
  • --schema(명령별): --body 페이로드에 대한 JSON 스키마.

종료 코드는 텍스트를 파싱하지 않고도 에이전트에게 무엇이 잘못되었는지 알려줍니다. 0은 정상, 1은 런타임 또는 API 실패, 2는 사용법 또는 검증 오류, 3은 인증입니다. 한 가지 주의점이 있습니다. 스트리밍 명령(generate, agent run)은 -o json이나 --jq가 단일 파싱 가능한 결과를 주려면 --stream=false가 필요합니다.

코딩 에이전트에 Gemini API CLI 제공하기

Google의 README에는 AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md 또는 .cursorrules에 붙여 넣을 블록이 있습니다. 발췌하면 다음과 같습니다:

You have access to gemini-api through the shell.
1. Inspect --help or --usage to choose a command, and --schema when building a --body JSON payload.
2. Preview API calls with --dry-run.
3. For JSON output or --jq on streaming commands, pass --stream=false --output-format json.
4. Capture returned file paths and interaction IDs to continue multi-step tasks.

GEMINI_API_KEY가 에이전트의 서브프로세스 환경에 전달되는지 확인하세요. 그런 다음 평소처럼 프롬프트를 입력하세요: "랜딩 페이지를 만들고, 마스코트 이미지와 20초 보이스오버에는 Gemini를 사용하고, 경쟁 제품에 대한 Deep Research 실행을 시작해 줘." 그러면 에이전트가 명령을 선택합니다.

하지 않는 것도 있습니다. 실시간 음성이나 비디오입니다. WebSocket 지원이 없으므로 Live API는 여전히 GenAI SDK가 필요합니다.

Apidog CLI로 직접 만든 API 테스트하기

gemini-api는 에이전트에게 Gemini의 모델을 제공합니다. 하지만 당신의 자체 API — 앱이 Gemini를 감싸는 /summarize나 /thumbnail 엔드포인트, 그 환경, 또는 릴리스가 깨지지 않았음을 입증하는 검증 — 에 대해서는 아무것도 모릅니다. 그것이 Apidog CLI의 일이며, 같은 에이전트가 둘 다 실행할 수 있습니다.

한 번 설정하세요:

npm install -g apidog-cli@latest
apidog login --with-token <YOUR_TOKEN>
npx -y skills add https://apidog.com   # pick your agent when prompted

그런 다음 에이전트에게 하나의 프롬프트를 주세요:

Use gemini-api to dry-run an analyze call on ./docs/sample-invoice.pdf, then run it for real.
Import ./openapi.yaml into Apidog project <id>, create a test case for POST /v1/invoices/extract
that uploads the same PDF and asserts a 200 and a non-empty "total" field, run it against the
staging environment, and summarize any failures.

에이전트는 gemini-api로 Gemini의 답변을 확인한 다음, Apidog 스키마를 읽고 페이로드를 작성하며, 이를 검증하고 케이스를 생성하고 실행합니다:

apidog import --project <id> --format openapi --file ./openapi.yaml
apidog cli-schema get test-case-create
apidog cli-schema validate test-case-create --file case.json
apidog test-case create --project <id> --file case.json
apidog run --test-case <caseId> --project <id> -e <envId> -r cli,json

apidog test-case create --help는 한 가지 함정을 알려줍니다. 케이스에는 유효한 categoryId가 필요하므로, 먼저 apidog test-case category --project <id>로 목록을 확인하세요. -r cli,json을 -r junit으로 바꾸면 같은 줄이 CI에서 실행됩니다. Claude Code를 에이전트로 사용한다면 Claude Code에서 Apidog CLI 사용하기부터 시작하세요. Apidog의 무료 플랜은 최대 4명의 사용자까지 지원합니다.

FAQ

Gemini API CLI는 무료인가요? CLI 자체는 Apache 2.0에 따라 무료이자 오픈소스입니다. 모든 호출은 일반적인 Gemini API 가격에 따라 당신의 API 키로 청구됩니다. 무료 티어가 무엇을 포함하는지는 Gemini API 무료 티어 가이드를 참고하세요.

gemini-api는 Gemini CLI와 같은 건가요? 아닙니다. Gemini CLI는 대화형 코딩 에이전트입니다. gemini-api는 다른 에이전트, 스크립트, CI 작업이 Gemini 모델과 관리형 에이전트에 접근하기 위해 호출하는 상태 비저장 도구입니다.

API 키 없이 명령을 테스트할 수 있나요? 예. --dry-run은 명령을 검증하고 네트워크 호출이나 키체인 읽기 없이 정확한 요청을 출력합니다. 이 글의 모든 예제는 0.4.5에서 이 방식으로 확인했습니다.

14MB보다 큰 파일은 어떻게 처리하나요? gemini-api files upload <file> --wait를 실행하고, 반환된 files/<id>를 보관한 뒤, analyze, transcribe, generate, image, video 또는 agent run의 -i에 전달하세요. 업로드는 48시간 후에 만료됩니다.

버전을 고정해야 하나요? 예, CI에서는 고정하세요. Google은 CLI가 베타인 동안 마이너 버전 간에 호환성을 깨는 변경이 발생할 수 있다고 밝혔습니다.

title: CVE-2026-105483: when an IPv4 address is checked as a DNS name
description:
CVE-2026-105483: when an IPv4 address is checked as a DNS name

Node.js applications often treat an IP address as the least ambiguous destination possible. CVE-2026-105483 shows why that assumption deserves scrutiny. In affected 24.x and 26.x releases, tls.checkServerIdentity() can evaluate a host written with fullwidth digits as a DNS name even though the same host normalizes and resolves to an IPv4 address. A certificate containing a matching DNS subject alternative name can then authenticate the connection without an IP address SAN.

The Node.js project published the fix in 24.22.1 and 26.12.1 on October 21, 2026. It rates the bug High. The GitHub advisory records CVSS v3.0 7.4 with network access, high attack complexity, no privileges or user interaction, and high confidentiality and integrity impact. The weakness is CWE-295, improper certificate validation.

The identity mismatch

TLS hostname verification asks a narrower question than DNS resolution. The client must decide what kind of identity it intended to contact, then compare the peer certificate with that identity. For a name, a DNS SAN is appropriate. For an IP address, the certificate should carry a matching IP address SAN.

The vulnerable path classified a fullwidth-digit host as something other than an IP address. It still normalized and resolved the host as IPv4. Verification then checked DNS names and the certificate Common Name. An attacker who can present a trusted certificate with a numeric DNS SAN could therefore satisfy the wrong identity check.

This is a regression introduced after the fix for CVE-2026-48618. The relevant distinction isn't whether the connection eventually uses TCP over IPv4. It is whether certificate verification understands that the endpoint is an IP address at the point where identity policy is applied.

Conditions for exploitation

Several conditions must align:

  • The client runs an affected Node.js 24.x or 26.x release.
  • The application connects to a host represented with fullwidth digits.
  • The host resolves to the IPv4 endpoint controlled by, or reachable by, the attacker.
  • The server certificate chains to a CA trusted by the client.
  • The certificate contains a DNS SAN matching the normalized address, such as 127.0.0.1 or an applicable wildcard, and no matching IP SAN is required.

An internet-facing Node.js process is not automatically vulnerable. The application must place the affected hostname flow in a security-relevant path. Common examples include user-supplied callback URLs, connector configuration, proxy targets, or integrations that accept destination addresses from another system. A hard-coded DNS name with ordinary TLS handling may never exercise the bug.

Impact

Successful exploitation defeats the identity binding TLS is expected to provide. The client can establish a session with an unintended endpoint while treating the peer certificate as valid. That can expose request data, credentials carried inside the session, and response integrity. The advisory assigns high confidentiality and integrity impact, though availability impact is absent.

The existence of a trusted certificate does not imply that the attacker is a public CA or that every internal CA is affected in the same way. The practical question is whether the client trusts a certificate chain that contains the attacker's chosen identity. Internal PKI, test CAs, and delegated certificate issuance can alter that answer.

Affected scope

The official advisory limits affected versions to Node.js 24.x before 24.22.1 and 26.x before 26.12.1. The same October release also fixed issues in the 22.x line, but this CVE is not listed as affecting 22.x. Teams should read the full release notes instead of applying one version rule to every CVE from that date.

Applications that share a supported but older runtime through containers, embedded runtimes, or managed build images need the same check. A package manifest can say one version while the deployed process executes another. Record the runtime reported by the actual process and the image digest used to deploy it.

Exposure context

On November 2, 2026 at 04:17 +08:00, ZoomEye Search app="Node.js" returned 5,539,674 product-fingerprint matches. Filter vul.cve="CVE-2026-105483" returned zero. Exposure is the larger selected count and represents Node.js fingerprints, not confirmed vulnerable deployments.

That distinction matters for prioritization. The count can help identify a broad technology population, but it cannot establish the running version, the application's TLS destination policy, or the trust anchors in use. Version and code-path evidence remain necessary.

Remediation

Upgrade to Node.js 24.22.1 or 26.12.1, or a later release on a supported line. Rebuild container images and redistributed binaries so old runtimes are not reintroduced during deployment. Verify the runtime inside the running application and the build artifact, not just the source dependency declaration.

As a temporary reduction measure, reject user-controlled non-ASCII host strings and require canonical ASCII DNS names or canonical IPv4 addresses before the TLS client is invoked. This can narrow the affected input path, but it is not a substitute for the patched runtime. Review custom certificate verification callbacks because bypassing the standard check can preserve a separate identity flaw.

Assurance

Add a regression test with an isolated test CA and a certificate that contains a numeric DNS SAN but no matching IP SAN. The fixed runtime should reject that certificate when the destination is an IP endpoint. Test the deployed binary, not only application code, and retain the fixture so a future dependency rollback fails visibly.

References

  • Node.js October 21, 2026 Security Releases
  • Node.js 24.22.1 release notes
  • Node.js 26.12.1 release notes
  • GitHub Advisory GHSA-8h4p-qpcq-gq24
  • ZoomEye Search

title: Python Quick Quiz CLI: Lightweight CLI Tool for Beginner Python Learning
description:
Python Quick Quiz CLI is a small command-line application that quizzes users on fundamental Python concepts. Each question covers a single topic such as variables, control flow, functions, or lists, and the program provides instant feedback along with a brief explanation of the correct answer. The tool is intentionally lightweight: it runs in a terminal, requires no external dependencies beyond the standard library, and can be executed with a single command.

The target audience is anyone starting out with Python who wants a quick way to test their knowledge without the overhead of a full IDE or interactive notebook. It’s also handy for instructors who want a reproducible quiz format for in‑class exercises or for self‑study during commutes.

To use the tool, clone the repository, navigate to the script folder, and run python quick_quiz.py. The program will prompt you with a series of multiple‑choice questions, accept your answer, and immediately tell you whether you were correct. If you missed a question, the explanation will help you understand the mistake.

Try it out and see how a few minutes of practice can reinforce your Python fundamentals.
Python Quick Quiz CLI

title: Part 2: I Broke Out of YouTube My Bot Now Hits Instagram & Twitter/X Too (3 Platforms, 3 Completely Different Protection Models)
description:
📖 Part 1 is here — read it first:
How I Built a Telegram Bot That Downloads YouTube Music & Videos (Up to 2 GB)

🤖 Try the live bot: (https://t.me/songsuperzxbot)
📦 Source code: github.com/chandan0000001/music-video_telegrambot

Someone sent me a message after Part 1 went live.

"Can it do Instagram Reels?"

Short answer at the time: no.

Slightly longer answer after a few weeks of work: yes, and also Twitter/X, and also Instagram Stories, profile pictures, highlights, and posts. But getting there was a completely different problem from YouTube — and I mean completely different. Three platforms. Three protection models. Three sets of rules about what you can fetch without authentication, what you can't, and what will quietly rate-limit you into oblivion if you're not careful.

This is the story of how I expanded the bot, what I learned about how Instagram and Twitter/X actually protect their content, and the architectural changes that come with supporting multiple platforms in one bot.

What the Bot Already Does (Quick Recap)

Before I get into the new stuff — if you haven't read Part 1, the short version:

The bot is a production-grade Telegram bot built with Python 3.11, aiogram 3, FFmpeg, and SQLite WAL mode. It searches YouTube, lets users pick from the top 5 results, and downloads audio in MP3/M4A/WAV up to 320kbps or video in MP4 up to 1080p. The clever parts are:

  • yt-dlp's Signature Cipher bypass — reverse-engineers YouTube's JS player to reconstruct the real stream URL
  • Smart 2 GB delivery — files under 48 MB go via HTTP Bot API instantly; larger files use native MTProto
  • Intel VAAPI hardware acceleration — FFmpeg transcodes using the GPU render node, ~10x faster than CPU
  • Full admin panel — stats, ban/unblock, broadcast, CSV export, live queue view
  • 30 automated tests — URL validation, FFmpeg pipeline, rate limiting, cancellation, database

That foundation is what Part 2 is built on. Now let's talk about why adding Instagram and Twitter/X was harder than just "swap yt-dlp's input URL."

Why Three Platforms is an Architecture Problem, Not Just a Feature

When I built the YouTube handler, it was a one-platform world. The whole flow assumed: user sends query or YouTube URL → validate → download → deliver.

The moment you add Instagram and Twitter/X, that assumption breaks. You now need:

  1. A URL router — detect which platform a URL belongs to before doing anything else
  2. Platform-specific authentication — Instagram requires a session cookie; YouTube needs cookies for age-restricted content; Twitter/X can sometimes do without
  3. Platform-specific content types — YouTube has audio or video. Instagram has reels, stories, highlights, posts, and profile pictures. Twitter/X has videos, images, and posts with mixed media
  4. Platform-specific rate limiting — YouTube is relatively forgiving. Instagram will silently downgrade your requests or temporarily block your IP if you hammer it. Twitter/X has changed its protection model more aggressively than any other platform in recent years

Here's the new routing layer that runs before any download starts:

import re
from enum import Enum

class Platform(Enum):
    YOUTUBE  = "youtube"
    INSTAGRAM = "instagram"
    TWITTER  = "twitter"
    UNKNOWN  = "unknown"

PLATFORM_PATTERNS = {
    Platform.YOUTUBE: re.compile(
        r'^https?://(www\.)?(youtube\.com/watch\?v=|youtu\.be/|youtube\.com/shorts/)[A-Za-z0-9_\-]{11}'
    ),
    Platform.INSTAGRAM: re.compile(
        r'^https?://(www\.)?instagram\.com/(p|reel|stories|tv|s)/[A-Za-z0-9_\-]+'
    ),
    Platform.TWITTER: re.compile(
        r'^https?://(www\.)?(twitter\.com|x\.com)/\w+/status/\d+'
    ),
}

def detect_platform(url: str) -> Platform:
    # SSRF guard — always first
    if re.match(r'https?://(localhost|127\.|10\.|192\.168\.|169\.254\.)', url):
        return Platform.UNKNOWN
    for platform, pattern in PLATFORM_PATTERNS.items():
        if pattern.match(url):
            return platform
    return Platform.UNKNOWN

The SSRF check runs before platform detection. An attacker sending http://192.168.1.1/admin disguised as any platform URL gets rejected at this layer, not inside any platform-specific handler.

Platform 1: YouTube (The One We Already Solved)

Covered in full in Part 1. The short summary of how YouTube protects streams:

  • Signature Cipher — stream URLs are scrambled via a JavaScript function that yt-dlp reverse-engineers from YouTube's player JS
  • n-parameter throttle — download speed is capped at ~50 KB/s unless you decrypt an "n" parameter from the same JS bundle
  • po_token — a newer proof-of-origin token embedded in browser sessions, requiring a valid cookies.txt to bypass

yt-dlp handles all three. Keep it updated and refresh cookies.txt every few weeks.

Platform 2: Instagram — Sessions, Stories, and Aggressive Rate Limiting

Instagram's protection model is fundamentally different from YouTube's. YouTube obfuscates stream URLs but serves them publicly. Instagram ties almost everything to authenticated sessions.

What's public vs what needs auth

No authentication needed:

  • Public post images and videos
  • Public Reels
  • Profile pictures (always public — served directly from Instagram's CDN)

Requires a valid Instagram session:

  • Stories (expire in 24 hours; private to logged-in users)
  • Highlights (archived stories; account-level access)
  • Content from private accounts

How Instagram serves content

When you watch a Reel in your browser, the actual video file is served from Instagram's CDN — URLs that look like:

https://scontent-iad3-1.cdninstagram.com/v/t50.2886-16/...?_nc_ht=scontent...&_nc_cat=...

These CDN URLs are time-limited and session-tied. They're embedded inside a JSON blob in the page's JavaScript bundle or fetched via an internal GraphQL endpoint. yt-dlp's Instagram extractor reverse-engineers these endpoints to pull the direct CDN URL.

For authenticated content (stories, highlights), the extractor needs a valid sessionid cookie — the same session token your browser uses when you're logged into Instagram.

Configuring Instagram in the bot 

def get_instagram_opts(content_type: str, output_path: str) -> dict:
    base_opts = {
        'outtmpl': output_path,
        'quiet': True,
        'cookiefile': 'instagram_cookies.txt',  # must contain valid sessionid
        'http_headers': {
            'User-Agent': 'Mozilla/5.0 (X11; Linux x86_64) AppleWebKit/537.36',
        },
    }

    if content_type in ('reel', 'video', 'post'):
        base_opts['format'] = 'bestvideo[ext=mp4]+bestaudio[ext=m4a]/best[ext=mp4]'
    elif content_type == 'story':
        base_opts['format'] = 'best'  # stories are single-stream
    elif content_type == 'profile_picture':
        base_opts['format'] = 'best'

    return base_opts

The rate limiting trap

Instagram rate-limits by IP and by session. If you download too many items in quick succession using the same session cookie, Instagram starts returning 401 Unauthorized errors — even for public content — or silently serves lower-quality versions.

My fix: per-platform cooldown timers. Instagram downloads enforce a 15-second minimum gap between requests from the same session. This is longer than the YouTube cooldown (10 seconds) specifically because Instagram's rate limiting is less forgiving and harder to detect when it's happening.

PLATFORM_COOLDOWNS = {
    Platform.YOUTUBE:   10,   # seconds between requests
    Platform.INSTAGRAM: 15,   # Instagram rate-limits harder
    Platform.TWITTER:   8,
}

Profile pictures — the easy one

Profile pictures are the simplest Instagram download. They're always public, always served directly from the CDN, and don't require authentication:

https://instagram.com/{username}/?__a=1

The JSON response contains graphql.user.profile_pic_url_hd — a direct image URL. No cipher, no session required, just a clean HTTP GET.

Platform 3: Twitter/X — Bearer Tokens and a Platform That Keeps Moving

Twitter's 2023 pivot to X — and the dramatic changes to API access that came with it — made this the most technically interesting platform to support.

How Twitter/X protects video content

Twitter/X video is delivered as HLS streams (HTTP Live Streaming). When you watch a video in a tweet, the player fetches an M3U8 playlist that lists the actual video segments:

#EXTM3U
#EXT-X-VERSION:3
#EXT-X-STREAM-INF:BANDWIDTH=2176000,RESOLUTION=1280x720
https://video.twimg.com/ext_tw_video/.../720x1280/...m3u8
#EXT-X-STREAM-INF:BANDWIDTH=832000,RESOLUTION=640x360
https://video.twimg.com/ext_tw_video/.../360x640/...m3u8

The M3U8 playlist URL itself is embedded in the tweet's card data, which is fetched from an internal API endpoint:

https://api.twitter.com/1.1/statuses/show.json?id=<tweet_id>

This endpoint requires a Bearer token — an authentication token that Twitter's own web client sends with every request. yt-dlp extracts this bearer token from Twitter/X's JavaScript bundle (the same approach it uses for YouTube's cipher — find the token in the JS, use it for requests).

What happened in 2023

When Elon Musk took over Twitter and rebranded it to X, free API tier access was almost entirely removed. Third-party apps that relied on Twitter's public API were killed. Nitter (the privacy-friendly Twitter frontend) started failing. Many download tools broke.

yt-dlp adapted by switching to the "guest API" — an unauthenticated path that Twitter/X still exposes for public content, using a guest token that gets issued when you visit the site without being logged in. This guest token approach still works for public tweets.

Handling tweets with multiple images

A tweet can have 1-4 images. When a user sends a tweet URL with multiple images, the bot downloads all of them and sends them as a Telegram media group:

async def handle_twitter_images(url: str, message: Message):
    with yt_dlp.YoutubeDL({'quiet': True, 'skip_download': True}) as ydl:
        info = ydl.extract_info(url, download=False)

    if 'entries' in info:
        # Multiple images — send as album
        media_group = []
        for entry in info['entries']:
            img_url = entry.get('url')
            if img_url:
                media_group.append(InputMediaPhoto(media=img_url))

        if media_group:
            await message.answer_media_group(media=media_group)
    else:
        # Single image or video
        ...

Telegram supports sending up to 10 items in a media group, which covers Twitter/X's 4-image maximum comfortably.

The Content-Type Detection System

Instagram URLs carry information about content type in the path:

URL pattern Content type
instagram.com/p/{id}/ Post (image or video)
instagram.com/reel/{id}/ Reel (short video)
instagram.com/stories/{user}/{id}/ Story
instagram.com/s/{highlight_id}/ Highlight
instagram.com/{username}/ Profile (→ profile picture)
instagram.com/tv/{id}/ IGTV (long video) 
def detect_instagram_content_type(url: str) -> str:
    if '/reel/' in url:    return 'reel'
    if '/stories/' in url: return 'story'
    if '/p/' in url:       return 'post'
    if '/s/' in url:       return 'highlight'
    if '/tv/' in url:      return 'video'
    # If it's just instagram.com/{username}/ — profile picture
    if re.match(r'https?://(www\.)?instagram\.com/[^/]+/?$', url):
        return 'profile_picture'
    return 'unknown'

The bot surfaces a different keyboard to the user depending on content type. A Reel shows "Download Video" and "Download Audio". A Story just shows "Download". A profile URL shows "Download Profile Picture". No unnecessary choices for things that have only one format.

Updated Supported Platforms

Here's where the bot stands now:

Platform Content Types Auth Required
YouTube Music search, Audio (MP3/M4A/WAV), Video (144p–1080p) cookies.txt (age-restricted only)
Instagram Reel, Video, Post, Story, Highlight, Profile Picture sessionid cookie (stories/highlights)
Twitter / X Video, Post images (up to 4), GIF None (public tweets)

All three platforms route through the same pipeline:
URL → platform detection → SSRF guard → content type detection → platform-specific yt-dlp config → FFmpeg → smart delivery (HTTP or MTProto) → cleanup.

What I Learned Building This

Instagram is the hardest platform to stay compatible with. YouTube breaks when they rotate the cipher — that's a known, predictable event that yt-dlp patches. Instagram breaks when they change their internal GraphQL schema, which happens without announcement and with no public documentation to reference. Two of my three "bot is down" incidents since adding Instagram support were Instagram schema changes, not YouTube.

Twitter/X's guest API is fragile. It works today. X has shown zero interest in maintaining compatibility with third-party tools, and the guest API could be deprecated at any point. I handle this by catching yt-dlp errors and returning a clear message to users — "this video may not be downloadable" — instead of silently failing.

Per-platform rate limiting is non-negotiable. A single rate limiter across all platforms was my first approach. It was wrong. Instagram needs longer cooldowns than YouTube. Twitter/X is somewhere in the middle. Platform-specific cooldown values aren't premature optimization — they're the difference between a bot that works reliably and one that gets session-banned after 20 minutes.

yt-dlp is genuinely impressive. One library, three completely different platform protection models, maintained by a community that ships patches sometimes within hours. The right posture when building on top of it: keep it updated, wrap all extractor calls in robust error handling, and never assume a config that works today will work in two weeks.

Try It

The bot handles all three platforms now. Drop a YouTube link, an Instagram Reel, or a Twitter/X video URL and it figures out the rest.

Try it: @songsuperzxbot

Source code: github.com/chandan0000001/music-video_telegrambot

Part 1 (YouTube deep-dive): dev.to/chandan0000001/...

Questions about Instagram's session handling, Twitter/X's HLS parsing, or anything else — drop them in the comments.
